newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stks end off as foreign investors track US.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stks end off as foreign investors track US.

text.p: Caracas stocks closed down for the second day running as local investors stood back for lack of foreign investors, who continued to be drawn by soaring U.S. shares, traders said.
"The bolsa continues to fall for lack of investors," said Interacciones broker Piero Montelli. "And it looks as though prices have not yet hit a floor and will continue adjusting," he added.
The market's leading 19-share index slumped 1.29 percent to close at 6,365.67 points as 18 million shares, worth two billion bolivars ($4.25 million), traded.
"Local players have not been enough, alone, to support the market," said another broker.

Among traded issues 32 fell, seven rose and six closed flat. Market leader Electricidad de Caracas closed off 8.50 bolivars at 481.00 bolivars while national telephone company CANTV slipped 7.00 bolivars to end at 1930.00.
CANTV workers threatened Tuesday to strike after rejecting a "petty" 20 percent pay offer.
Venezuela began the year with waves of labor unrest led by a nationwide doctors strike.
Doctors accepted a 164 percent pay increase Tuesday, after rejecting an initial 25 percent pay offer, but refused to call off the strike until other benefits were settled.
Analysts fear continuing steep wage demands may throw a delicate fiscal balance out of wack, jeopardizing the government's 25 percent inflation target for 1997.
